source.title: The information bottleneck method
source.venue: Proceedings of the 37th Annual Allerton Conference on Communication, Control and Computing

confidence_rationale: The IB defines relevant information only relative to a chosen relevance variable Y: the optimal compression of X depends on Y, so there is no Y-free notion of what must be kept. That is formal backing for the idea that what crosses a boundary depends on the consumer's task, which is ARC-144's core. Held low because the IB is a formal definition, not evidence about brains or REE; it is motivational for the per-boundary indexing and does not by itself show that obligations differ across real interfaces or that a shared core is small.
failure_signatures: Reading 'relevance is relative to Y' as evidence that real cognitive interfaces have different obligation sets; the IB only says they would if their consumers' relevance variables differ.
The IB assumes the joint p(x,y) is known and the decoder unconstrained; it measures information-theoretic, not operational, sufficiency -- exactly the standard GOV-CONTRACT-3 rules inadmissible.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Relevant information in a signal X is defined as the information it carries about another variable Y; the optimal compressed representation T minimises I(T;X) subject to preserving I(T;Y), with a trade-off parameter, and the solution depends on the choice of Y.
mapping.ree_translation: For a handoff A -> B, take Y to be the variables B's task needs. Then I_AB is (roughly) the IB-relevant part of A's state for Y_B, and two receivers with different Y give different optimal payloads. This is the cleanest formal statement of 'boundary-indexed, not one universal header'.
mapping.mapping_caveat: ARC-144 defines I_AB as what B needs and CANNOT CHEAPLY RECONSTRUCT locally; the IB has no term for receiver-side resources or side information (see Wyner-Ziv entry for that). The IB also counts Shannon information with an ideal decoder, which GOV-CONTRACT-3 explicitly refuses as a reduction standard. So it supports ARC-144's framing and is at best a starting formalism for GOV-CONTRACT-3's cost, not a validation of it.
mapping.source_context: Foundational information-theory paper introducing the IB as a variational principle generalising rate-distortion with a relevance-defined distortion.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical and correct as mathematics; mapping is conceptual; transfer to a neural/agent substrate unmeasured. Metadata verified by WebSearch hits (arXiv physics/0004057, Allerton 1999 pp. 368-377); publisher/arXiv pages were egress-blocked in this session, so no DOI is given.
